verses.1: And some people who came from Judea taught their brothers that if they did not follow the laws of Moses, they would not be able to be saved.
verses.2: Due to this situation and the urgent nature of the request, Paul and Barnabas decided to go back to Jerusalem with some of their followers and other representatives, in order to discuss this matter with the apostles.
verses.3: Those who were warned by the church then went to Phoenicia and Samaria, describing the return of the nations. They brought great joy to all their brothers.
verses.4: But when they arrived in Jerusalem, they were received by the church, by the apostles, and by the elders. They also reported everything that God had done through them.
verses.5: Some of those who were influenced by the teachings of the Pharisees said that it was necessary to follow Moses’ laws and regulations.
verses.6: The apostles and the elders also gathered together to hear about this message.
verses.7: After many requests were made, Peter stood up and said to them, “Brothers, you must know that God has chosen me to listen to the words of the gospel from your mouths, so that you may believe in them, even though for thousands of years, no one else has had the opportunity to do this.”
verses.8: And the god of hearts also condemned them, giving them the holy spirit, just as he did to us.
verses.9: And surely, they did not distinguish between us and them, after they had purified their hearts.
verses.10: Now then, what are you trying to do by attacking the god? After all, it’s just a weight that can be placed on the necks of our students. Neither our fathers nor we have ever been able to bring it down.
verses.11: But because of the grace of our Lord Jesus, we believe that we can be saved in the same way as those others.
verses.12: Then all the crowd gathered together. Barnabas and Paul explained to them what God had done through these people, and the signs and wonders that He had performed among them.
verses.13: After they had quieted down, Jacob said, “Men, brothers, listen to me.”
verses.14: He explained that, as originally, the god wanted to take a people from various nations under his own name.
verses.15: And in this, the words of the prophets agree, as they are written.
verses.16: After this, I will rearrange and repair the stage of David’s statue. I will also repair and correct any damages that have occurred to it.
verses.17: So that those who are worthy of it may be called by my name. And all the nations on which my name is mentioned will be included in this list, says the Lord who does these things.
verses.19: Therefore, I consider it inappropriate to disturb those who return from other nations in order to worship the God.
verses.20: But they should also be aware of the dangers associated with the masks, as well as prostitution, bloodshed, and other such things.
verses.21: For Moises, by his ancient lineage, has those who preach his teachings in the city, and he spends every Saturday attending to them.
verses.22: Then it was decided by the apostles and the elders, along with all those who were chosen from the church, to send Paul and Barnabas to Antioch. They also sent Judas, who was called Barsabas, and Silas. These men were considered among the brothers.
verses.23: Written by their own hands. The apostles and the elders greet those in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia, as well as those from other nations.
verses.24: Because we heard that some of us who left here disturbed you with their words, trying to deceive your souls, which we did not allow.
verses.25: He wished to send to you, along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, those men who were chosen as his companions.
verses.26: They will give their souls over to us in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.27: We therefore sent Judas and Silvan to them, and we told them the same things through words.
verses.28: For the holy spirit would not allow us to burden you any further than this.
verses.29: Avoid temples, as well as blood, smoke, and prostitution. From these things, you should abstain. Be virtuous.
verses.30: Those who were dismissed went to Antiochean. They gathered together the crowd and gave them the letter.
verses.31: But when they read the instructions, they were pleased with them.
verses.32: Eudas and Silas, who were also prophets, through many words, called upon their brothers and asked for their help.
verses.33: After a while, they were released in peace by their brothers, who had sent them there.
verses.35: Pavlos and Barnabas also preached and proclaimed the word of the Lord in Antioch, along with many other people.
verses.36: After a few days, he said to Barnabas, “When we returned, we went to visit our brothers in the city where we had brought up the matter before the Lord. We wanted to see how they were doing.”
verses.37: But Barnabas also wanted to take along John, who was known as Mark.
verses.38: But Paul, who was a wise man, refused to leave them at Pamphlia, and he didn’t go with them on this task. He didn’t want to take part in this.
verses.39: It happened that they were separated from each other. Barnabas took Mark with him and went to Cyprus.
verses.40: Pauros, having been chosen as a leader by Silanus, went away to obey the commands of his lord, under the leadership of his brothers.
verses.41: He also traveled through Syria and Cilicia, visiting various churches along the way.
